decisions.reason: As a flagship launch tied closely to the firm's announced move toward broader cloud-based enterprise messaging, management is likely to continue backing it and interpret any remaining shortfalls as market-development rather than product failure.
Because it extends the established document workflow business and reflects prior R&D and launch investment, management is inclined to keep it and justify continued support rather than reverse course.

Its public visibility is lower, but as an adjacent messaging service using existing capabilities and serving legacy communication needs, management would still be more likely to retain it than abandon it.

This is the easiest of the four to cut because it is a narrower, less visible feature, yet its fit with the firm's regulated communications base and the tendency to defend earlier incremental investments still favor keeping it for now.
